facts.hook: In 1932, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns against emus
facts.body: In late 1932, the army ran a wildlife-control operation in Western Australia. Major Meredith led two soldiers armed with two Lewis guns and 10,000 rounds of ammunition.

facts.hook: By his own report, Major Meredith used exactly ten rounds per emu killed
facts.body: Meredith's report claimed 986 confirmed kills with 9,860 rounds. The media adopted the name "Emu War" for the operation.

facts.hook: In 1919, a molasses wave at an estimated 35 mph swept through Boston
facts.body: On January 15, 1919, a molasses tank burst in Boston's North End. The wave rushed through the streets at an estimated 35 mph (56 km/h), killing 21 people and injuring 150.

facts.hook: In 1962, laughter spread to 95 of 159 pupils at a school in Tanganyika
facts.body: It began on January 30, 1962, with three girls at a mission-run boarding school in Kashasha. It was an outbreak of mass hysteria, and the school had to close on March 18.

facts.hook: In 1858, the Thames stench led Parliament to soak its curtains in chemicals
facts.body: During the hot summer of 1858, the smell of untreated waste from the Thames got so bad that business in Parliament was affected. The curtains were soaked in lime chloride to fight the stench.

facts.hook: London fought cholera by removing a smell, and it worked for a different reason
facts.body: The smell from the Thames was thought to spread disease. Bazalgette's sewers stopped sewage being dumped on the river's shores and ended the cholera outbreaks; cholera was later accepted to be water-borne, not spread by miasma.

facts.hook: Modern scholars say the tulip bubble was less destructive than the legend
facts.body: Charles Mackay's 1841 book claimed many investors were ruined. Many modern scholars believe the mania was not as destructive as he described; scholar Anne Goldgar says it was limited to "a fairly small group".

facts.hook: A rainy summer in 1816 led to Frankenstein and The Vampyre
facts.body: In June 1816, incessant rain kept Mary Shelley, Byron, Polidori and friends indoors at Villa Diodati on their Swiss holiday. Byron proposed a scary-story contest: Shelley wrote Frankenstein, and Polidori drew on a Byron fragment for The Vampyre.

facts.hook: A shortage of oats in 1816 may have inspired an early bicycle
facts.body: After the 1816 harvest failures, oats became scarce for horses. That may have led German inventor Karl Drais to look for horseless transport and to invent the draisine, a precursor of the bicycle.
